newsitem.title: UK: Brent cargo trades firmer at Aug Brent +4 cts.
newsitem.headline: Brent cargo trades firmer at Aug Brent +4 cts.

text.p: A cargo of North Sea Brent crude oil traded on Tuesday at a firmer August Brent +4 cent - four cents up from the low deal on Friday, traders said.
The August 12-14 loading cargo was sold by a trader to a refiner who had been thought short into another refiner.
Talk that one of the two August 13-15 Brent cargoes from Tuesday's paper chains had been kept and onsold could not be confirmed.
Traders expected the market to hold at current levels until the end of the week when many expected Dated Brent to fall quickly against August.
Otherwise the markets saw little action with levels slightly firmer as buying interest on paper markets saw sellers move off.

"It's deadly. There's been nothing done at all. Just talk on who is moving where," one trader said refering to market talk that two crude oil traders had officially quit a major oil company to join an international bank on Tuesday.
September Brent crude oil traded at 1200 GMT up 10 cents at $18.51 a barrel. Intermonth spreads saw the Aug/Sep valued around +14 cents though the best bid was heard at +10 cents.
Brent Sep/Oct talked -7/-3 cents while Oct/Nov was unchanged on the day at -12/-10 cents.
Brent CFD talk firmed up a few cents with the remainder of this week notionally assessed around Sept +10/+15 value, while Aug 4-8 talked Sept -8/-4 cents.
The second Brent cargo from Tuesday's paper chains was also being offered on the market by a refiner.
None of the July Brent barrels have been five o' clocked to date.
Other sweet grades were unchanged in value though here again talk was very limited.
